applies_why: The judge text addresses a challenger point pressed against a curse limb the defender dropped, so there is no live link and no chain-vs-chain collision for rule K-C to govern.
quote: C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: pressed against a link — (1) requires a live link still maintained, so a dropped limb triggers no K-C weighing; (2) includes a dropped limb if referenced, so K-C still governs.
why: Because the judge's stated ground is that the targeted curse limb was dropped, not that C4 lacks a contrary verse, the judge text does not do the verse-by-verse or stating-verse analysis K-C forbids.
